doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Fixing the parade route; Sergeant's push for senior band in front
summary: Edna and her secretary plan the parade route and she refuses the sergeant's request to change it.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: They led the parade, the Holy Family sisters.

Oh, they had to be top. Now, that's one thing I put my foot down on. They were fixing the roots of the parade. And so the Sergeant Aubrey, he had his men out there to tie the parade. And so, Ms. Bozamp, my secretary, and I, we fixed the roots of the parade. And I said, Ms. Senegal, I'll suit you. And I said, well, if you didn't like me, I said, all right, let's go over this thing again. All right. We took about, oh, from 8 to about 11 o'clock at night. We were going over that root, faced the bands and everything, where I wore them and everything. And the next night came Sergeant Aubrey. He's a nice fellow, all right. Oh, he's just so nice. But I had to get him straight now. So he was at Ms. Bozamp. And she called me. Ms. Senegal? Sergeant Aubrey's making a lot of changes with his root. I said, now listen, you want to keep me well, just don't tell me nothing about no changes. She says, but he says it has to be changed. And I says it will not be changed. And so we all get like that. I said, oh. She said, now what am I going to do with you two people? One say it has it. I said, now listen. I said, put Sergeant Aubrey on the phone. All right, lady, what's the matter? I said, can't you accept that root the way we have it for you? Can't you accept it the way it is? No, ma'am, I can't. I says, why? He says, because it's against the rules and regulations. I said, what rules and regulations? He says, something about, he didn't say police, he said something else. And I asked him, I said, against the rules and regulations of the police? Oh, no, no, no, no. I said, against the city, a vote or something? I said, you know, I have my permit for the parade. And it says on there what they allow, and I'm going to call them to the city regulations. Now, I respect you as an officer, but remember that route is mine. You're an officer, but that route is mine. Somebody said, now listen. I said, well, what do you mean by that? He said, well, you know, you have to put a senior band in front. You cannot put a senior band behind a junior band. Have you all, have you heard about that? Have you heard about that? No.
And I had never heard about that.

Huh? Well, he wanted to do that. All right. And so I said, no, I never heard of it. No, I never heard of it. He said, but, Ms. Senegal, won't you just let me change that? I said, you have several changes in that, not only one. I want it to be just as I have it. So he said, well, a senior band has to be front. Why? I said, why? He said, because they are senior and the others junior. I said, I didn't want to tell you this, but since you are persistent and asking me for it, I am going to tell you why. And I don't care if the world knows why. I say, St. Mary's band has been with us since 1952, since the beginning. The Holy Family Sisters have let that band play for us. Every year has never turned us down for nothing. But the St. Augustine's band have not. Oh, they haven't? I said, no. Three or four years they haven't been playing for us. He says, why? I said, well, I won't say why. I said, because that's personal. But they haven't been with us. Is that enough for you? He says, no, I want to know the reason why. I said, well, I'll not say it on the phone. The reason why. But they haven't been with us. But St. Mary's band was there with us and are still with us. And I want them first. Oh, he says, you have a reason. You have a reason. I said, yes, I have a reason. And he says, well, and something else he said. What is it, something else you find fault of?
